paras: The assault on Will Baker at Selma was an attack on a Black man by five or six young white men on the river bank opposite Selma, Alabama, on the afternoon of April 8, 1903. The men struck him, threw him into the river and threatened to cut his throat with a razor, but he survived.
The bank across from the city had lately become a gathering place for crap shooters.

At about 2 o'clock, residents on the city side saw one Black man and six young white men struggling. They saw him struck over the head and thrown into the river while one of the men brandished a large razor. He caught hold of tree limbs and called for help, and the men ran away.
Baker said he had stopped his boat to watch the men shooting craps, and that when he showed $3 they took it, struck him with a stick and threw him in the river.

Four young men were arrested at the ball park, but Baker said they had not been among his attackers, and the names of the others were said to be known to the authorities. No report of further arrests, charges or a trial appears in the coverage.

Selma dispatches ran on April 9 in the Montgomery Advertiser and the Birmingham Age-Herald; no Black-press coverage was found. The Age-Herald headed its story "NEGRO WON MONEY BUT GOT BEATING" and opened with a minstrel song, using a slur, about a Black man who won at cards and "was afraid to pick it up." The Advertiser printed Baker's account beside a "most credited" version, from people who were not eyewitnesses, in which he won the white men's money and was attacked for refusing to return it.

The Age-Herald named the victim Bill Barker; the Advertiser, which reported his own statement, called him Will Baker. Both papers described the attack as "this afternoon" in April 9 editions, so the Age-Herald's April 8 dateline is more likely than the Advertiser's April 9.

reader.title: Assault on Will Baker at Selma
bases: A group of five or six young white men struck a Black man, threw him into the river and threatened him with a razor; he survived and no killing is reported (A1, A2).

Two separately filed Selma reports, the Advertiser Bureau's and an Age-Herald special, agree on the core events of a Black man struck, thrown into the river and threatened with a razor by about six young white men (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Victim's account
accounts.gist: Baker said he stopped to watch six white men shooting craps; when asked if he had money he showed $3, and the men took it, struck him with a stick and threw him in the river while one threatened to cut his throat with a razor.

accounts.label: 'Most credited' story from people near the scene
accounts.gist: Baker asked to join the game, was allowed in, won all the money, refused to give it back, and was set upon and robbed; the men threw him in the river fearing trouble and might have killed him had they not been frightened away.

accounts.label: Onlookers across the river
accounts.gist: Residents on the city side saw one Black man and six young white men struggling; he was struck over the head and thrown into the river while one man brandished a razor, and the white men ran when he called for help.

framing.detail: The Montgomery Advertiser printed Baker's account and a competing 'most credited' version blaming the dispute on his winnings, while describing the men as having 'set upon' him and noting arrests.
The Birmingham Age-Herald treated the attack as comic, heading it 'NEGRO WON MONEY BUT GOT BEATING' and opening with a minstrel song using a slur, while describing a 'narrow escape'.

conflicts.note: Both reports appeared in April 9 papers; an afternoon event on the publication date of a morning paper is unlikely, so April 8 is the better-supported date.
The Advertiser gives his own account at length, which favors 'Will Baker'.
